premises.text: Social influences significantly impact product discovery and purchasing decisions.
premises.evidence_span: friends do help friends discover products.

premises.text: E-commerce has evolved to focus primarily on individual needs, making it a solitary experience.
premises.evidence_span: the experience has become very solitary, almost like a chore.

premises.text: Visual proof of people engaging with products enhances the shopping experience.
premises.evidence_span: real people looking at real products.

premises.text: Sneak Peek curates a personalized store based on user and friends' preferences.
premises.evidence_span: We use what you and your friends like on Sneak Peek to create a store every single day just for you.

premises.text: The Peek feature drops prices intelligently based on user engagement.
premises.evidence_span: every Peek drops the price for everyone peaking.

premises.text: Real-time social proof encourages users to make purchasing decisions.
premises.evidence_span: this adds the social proof we all need to move us from discovery to purchase.

premises.text: Game mechanics like competition and urgency drive sales.
premises.evidence_span: game mechanics, such as competition and urgency, really drive sales.

premises.text: Sneak Peek has established over 100 brand partnerships.

value.text: Users can discover and purchase products more effectively through social engagement.
value.evidence_span: the fact that I can discover something new is interesting.

notes: Pilot learnings and user engagement metrics are excluded as traction.
